examples.about: The editable standard examples and the failure examples, as model records of schema version 1 (src/record.js). Each variable, equation, condition and assumption has a stable id. Values are illustrative inputs for the example, not measured data.

examples.label: Convection: Pi groups
examples.title: Convective heat transfer: the worked Buckingham Pi calculation

purpose.question: On which independent dimensionless groups does the heat-transfer coefficient of a body in a flow depend?

geometry.domain: A body of characteristic length L in a uniform flow of speed U
geometry.coordinates: None, because the calculation uses the Pi variables only

assumptions.text: The inputs have no additional constraints.
k is the conductivity of the fluid, so hL/k is a Nusselt number and not a Biot number.

evidence.claim: The worked calculation gives rank 4 and the groups hL/k, μ/(ρUL) and ρc_pUL/k for the repeating variables ρ, U, L, k.

examples.label: Straight fin
examples.title: Straight fin with an insulated tip: the complete Pi basis

purpose.question: On which dimensionless groups does the base heat flow of a fin with a constant cross-section and an insulated tip depend?

variables.meaning: Heat flow at the fin base

geometry.domain: A straight fin of length L, constant cross-section A_c and exposed perimeter P
geometry.coordinates: x along the fin, from the base (x = 0) to the tip (x = L)
geometry.interfaces: The base at x = 0 and the insulated tip at x = L

assumptions.text: Temperature varies along x only. The transverse-conduction validity condition needs a separate derivation.

evidence.claim: The time row equals −3 times the mass row, the rank is 3 and the variable set has 4 independent groups.
m²L² = hPL²/(kA) is the fin parameter of the insulated-tip solution.

examples.label: Transient slab
examples.title: Transient slab with surface convection: the groups before nondimensionalization

purpose.question: On which dimensionless groups does the temperature depend in a slab that cools by convection at its surface?

variables.meaning: Local excess of temperature, T − T_∞
Initial excess of temperature, T_i − T_∞

geometry.domain: A slab of half-thickness L, symmetric about its centre plane
geometry.coordinates: x from the centre plane (x = 0) to the surface (x = L), and time t
geometry.interfaces: The surface at x = L, in contact with a fluid at T_∞

assumptions.text: The slab is symmetric about its centre plane.
T_i is not equal to T_∞.
ρ and c_p enter the equation only as ρc_p, so α = k/(ρc_p) replaces them in the Pi set.

evidence.claim: The slab conditions and the groups X, Fo = τ, θ and Bi.

quantities.about: The quantity vocabulary of the variable table. A variable may name one quantity; its dimension must agree with the unit and the dimension formula. Familiar groups (groups.json) match on these ids, never on symbols. temperature: absolute or difference. meaning: the physical meaning a dimensionless quantity keeps.

groups.about: Familiar dimensionless groups, each stored as formulas over quantities with explicit reference quantities, never as a name alone (spec section 10). A group matches a calculated group when one of its forms gives the same exponent for each supplied variable through a one-to-one match of quantities. phase, kind and role narrow a term: phase fluid or solid; kind parameter (the default, which also matches a constant), field, coordinate or any. A recognized name is a proposed interpretation until the researcher confirms it. Order is the preference order for a familiar basis.

groups.label: Nu
groups.name: Nusselt number
groups.reference: L is the characteristic length of the declared geometry and k_f is the fluid conductivity. State whether h and Nu are local or mean values.

groups.label: λ²
groups.name: fin parameter squared, with λ = mL
groups.reference: L is the fin length, P the exposed perimeter and A_c the cross-sectional area.

groups.label: Q̇L/(kA_cΔT)
groups.name: base heat flow in dimensionless form
groups.reference: ΔT = T_b − T_∞ is the base excess temperature and must not be 0.

groups.label: PL/A_c
groups.name: ratio of perimeter times length to cross-sectional area
groups.reference: A geometry ratio of the fin.

groups.label: A_c/L²
groups.name: ratio of cross-sectional area to length squared
groups.reference: A geometry ratio of the fin.

groups.label: Bi
groups.name: Biot number
groups.reference: Bi needs the Biot length L_c and the solid conductivity k_s. L_c = V/A_s is the half-thickness of a slab cooled on both faces, r/2 for a long cylinder and r/3 for a sphere. A spatial solution uses the half-thickness or the radius.

groups.label: θ
groups.name: normalized temperature
groups.reference: The two differences must share one reference temperature, such as T_∞. The reference difference must not be 0.

groups.label: X
groups.name: dimensionless position
groups.reference: x is the coordinate and L the length scale of the declared domain, such as the half-thickness.

groups.label: Fo
groups.name: Fourier number
groups.reference: α_s is the solid diffusivity and L_c the same length as in Bi. When t is the time coordinate, Fo is the dimensionless time.

groups.label: Re
groups.name: Reynolds number
groups.reference: U is the reference speed and L the characteristic length. Use the same L as in Nu when an identity combines them.

groups.label: Pr
groups.name: Prandtl number
groups.reference: Pr is a ratio of fluid properties. Take all properties at one reference temperature.

groups.label: Pe
groups.name: Péclet number
groups.reference: Pe = Re Pr only when Re and Pr use the same reference properties.

groups.label: St_h
groups.name: Stanton number
groups.reference: State whether h and St_h are local or mean values.

groups.label: Gr
groups.name: Grashof number
groups.reference: State whether ΔT is a positive scale or a signed difference.

groups.label: Ra
groups.name: Rayleigh number
groups.reference: Ra = Gr Pr only when both use the same reference properties.

groups.label: Ri
groups.name: bulk Richardson number
groups.reference: A bulk Richardson number. The gradient Richardson number is a different quantity.

groups.label: Ste
groups.name: Stefan number
groups.reference: State the phase of c_p and the temperature interval of ΔT.

groups.label: Ec
groups.name: Eckert number
groups.reference: ΔT is a positive scale.

groups.label: Br
groups.name: Brinkman number
groups.reference: Br = Pr Ec only when both use the same reference properties.

groups.label: Ma_T
groups.name: thermal Marangoni number
groups.reference: Ma_T is a positive magnitude. Keep the sign of dγ/dT separately.

groups.label: NTU
groups.name: number of transfer units
groups.reference: U_HX is the overall heat-transfer coefficient, not a speed.

groups.label: C_r
groups.name: capacity rate ratio
groups.reference: C = ṁ c_p for each stream.

groups.label: τ_opt
groups.name: optical thickness
groups.reference: κ_a is the absorption coefficient of the medium.

sources.about: Every source the page cites, with the date read and the words it supports. An evidence item on the page names one of these ids.

sources.title: Specification 6, section 3: model entry and validation
sources.supports: The checks before analysis. They find undefined symbols, units that disagree, conditions that are not there and open constitutive laws. They also check temperatures, domains, zero scales and dependent inputs.

sources.title: Specification 6, section 4: Dimensionless Number Finder
sources.supports: The dimension matrix, the exact rank, the kernel basis and the n − r groups. Also the repeating variables and the checks of the basis.

sources.title: Specification 6, section 5: worked Buckingham Pi calculation
sources.supports: The variables h, k, ρ, μ, c_p, U and L, with the matrix D, det D_R = −1 and rank 4. The groups hL/k, μ/(ρUL) and ρc_pUL/k, and the familiar basis Nu, Re, Pr.

sources.title: Specification 6, section 7: worked slab nondimensionalization
sources.supports: The slab equation, its symmetry, convection and initial conditions, and the variables X, τ = Fo and θ.

sources.title: Specification 6, section 10: heat-transfer definitions and the straight fin
sources.supports: The group definitions with their reference quantities, such as Nu, Bi, Fo, Re and Pr. The fin variables with rank 3 and 4 groups.

sources.title: MIT 2.25 Advanced Fluid Mechanics (Fall 2013): The Buckingham Pi Theorem in Dimensional Analysis
sources.supports: A set of n − r independent Pi groups, with r the rank (the note writes k for it). The note says: "this set of non-dimensional parameters is not unique. They are however independent and form a complete set." It also asks "can I vary all of these variables independently", and it says "Compare with experimental data!"

sources.title: COMSOL 6.3 Heat Transfer Module: Defining the Heat Transfer Coefficients
sources.supports: Nu_L = hL/k, Re_L = ρUL/μ, Pr = μC_p/k, Ra_L = Gr_L Pr, with L the characteristic length.

sources.title: MIT 16 Unified Engineering, thermodynamics notes, section 18.2: Heat Transfer From a Fin
sources.supports: m²L² = hPL²/(kA), the insulated-tip profile cosh(mL(1 − ξ))/cosh(mL) and the base heat flow Q̇/(√(kAhP)(T₀ − T∞)) = tanh(mL).
